items.title: An invertible module is the same thing as a finite locally free module of rank one, and its inverse is its dual
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the equivalence of three conditions on a module M over a ring R: that M be finite locally free of rank 1, that M be invertible, and that there exist an R-module N with M tensor_R N isomorphic to R, together with the identification of the N in the third condition as Hom_R(M, R) (source lines 36117-36127). The proof is a three-way cycle of implications plus a rank argument. It first takes N = Hom_R(M, R) and the evaluation map, shows the evaluation map is an isomorphism by reducing to localizations at which M becomes free and invoking a cover argument (proof lines 36130-36135). The equivalence of invertibility with the existence of an inverse module is then a statement about tensor functors forming a quasi-inverse pair, with essential surjectivity for the converse (proof lines 36138-36141). The final and substantive part deduces finite local freeness: from an isomorphism psi : M tensor_R N -> R and an element xi = sum x_i tensor y_i with psi(xi) = 1, the proof exhibits the automorphism x -> sum psi(x tensor y_i) x_i of M and factors it through R^{oplus n}, so that M is a direct summand of a finite free module, hence finite locally free; applying the same to N by symmetry and using M tensor_R N isomorphic to R forces both to have rank 1 (proof lines 36144-36166). The non-routine content is the factoring of an automorphism through a finite free module, which is what produces the direct summand.
